key_insight: Distill transformer global modeling into lightweight state-space model (SSM) blocks and combine them in a modular hybrid architecture to retain restoration quality while drastically reducing attention-induced latency on edge devices.
problem_solved: Attention-heavy transformers give strong global context for image restoration but are slow on mobile/edge hardware, especially for high-resolution inputs; the paper addresses how to achieve transformer-level restoration performance with much lower runtime cost.
method: Modular hybrid architecture that interleaves transformer blocks (for learning rich global priors) with SSM blocks (e.g., Mamba) for linear-time sequence modeling and low runtime overhead.
Transformer-to-SSM distillation where knowledge from trained transformer components is transferred into efficient SSM modules so they emulate attention behaviors without heavy kernels.
Edge-oriented design and deployment considerations (block selection, resolution-aware scheduling) to minimize latency on mobile accelerators while preserving restoration fidelity.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy high-quality image-restoration models on constrained devices by replacing costly attention with distilled SSMs, lowering inference latency and power use without major drops in visual performance.

paper_title: Edge-Efficient Image Restoration: Transformer Distillation into State-Space Models
paper_authors: Srinivas Soumitri Miriyala, Sowmya Vajrala, Sravanth Kodavanti, Vikram Nelvoy Rajendiran, Sharan Kumar Allur
